text: The Rip is a frustrating missed opportunity. It takes a golden premise and two of cinema’s best friends and buries them under a mountain of plot holes.
Little by little “The Rip” devolves into a b-the-numbers action flick. The cast is strong, but they’re at the mercy of the material.
Sure, the resolution is pretty standard, but this brings out some of the best of what Carnahan has proved to be able to deliver when he’s working in serious mode.

On paper, The Rip should have worked. Dirty cops. Stolen money. A Cuban-American city where corruption is so baked in, it comes with cafecito. That is not an invention. That is Miami. The problem is that The Rip is not actually in Miami.

"The Rip" is nothing new. That makes it sound bad, when it’s actually a very entertaining action-thriller. But the fact is that there’s nothing revolutionary or revelatory about writer/director Joe Carnahan’s latest film.

While Affleck burrows himself in the role of a blunt yet noble cop, it’s Damon who gives the best performance in the film as the Lieutenant who has to decide what to do and how to locate a snitch. They're aging like fine wine.
'The Rip' tears up the screen with Affleck, Damoon in a tense cop thriller.
It all sits on the most medium level of meat and potatoes genre fare without ever doing anything good, bad or weird enough to risk that watchable yet forgettable status.
Ludicrous and more than a little confusing, but... there’s mercifully little to complain about here. Your dad will love this, and you’ll have an okay time, too.
The Rip isn't going to be a cultural touchstone or stand out as the best movie in anyone's career, but it's certainly not a failure.
The Rip is a blunt, confident action-genre throwback of the sort American writer-director Joe Carnahan built his name on.
A mediocre entry in the already overcrowded dirty cop genre.

With all the talk about corrupt cops, we do get the impression that he [Ben Affleck] might not be one of them, but the film never expands upon JD [Ben Affleck] to give us more depth or insight into him.
In a world where there is no shortage of cop thrillers, The Rip is sheer popcorn entertainment from start to finish.
The Rip seems highly possible until its overblown climatic end, but even when it succumbs to the action thriller norms, it and the cast always keeps you thoroughly entertained.
Joe Carnahan's crime thriller feels like a nice throwback to '90s genre pictures, but it pulls a few too many punches.
"The Rip" is nothing you haven’t seen before, and you won’t care.
Affleck and Damon lean into their parts, though most of the rest of the cast, save Calle, hang in the orbit of their swagger.
Matt Damon and Ben Affleck reunite to show the world the importance of a good script, which this film completely lacks. [Full review in Spanish]

I was entertained, even if for the longest stretches I couldn’t have told you who was doing what to whom. Chalk it up as yet another twist in the tale of Matt ‘n’ Ben – two Yin/Yang talents who will be yoked together for eternity.
